extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare billing/coding professionals, health policy stakeholders, and other parties affected by IPPS/LTCH PPS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and respond to CMS's FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule, including proposed payment and policy changes for MS-DRG classifications, wage index updates, payment adjustments (DSH, low-volume, MDH), quality reporting requirements, and related programmatic proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDH program termination/transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the MDH program is not authorized by statute beyond December 31, 2026, beginning January 1, 2027, all hospitals that previously qualified for MDH status under section 1886(d)(5)(G) of the Act will no longer have MDH status and will be paid based on the IPPS Federal rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects the statutory extension through December 31, 2026 under section 6202 of the CAA, 2026; unless law changes, MDH status and related payment adjustments end after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital IPPS payment methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(g) requires Secretary to pay capital-related costs in accordance with a prospective payment system; basic methodology set forth at 42 CFR 412.308 and 412.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under capital IPPS, payments are adjusted by the same DRG as operating IPPS and adjusted for IME and DSH similarly; hospitals may also receive outlier payments for unusually high-cost cases; see 42 CFR part 412, subparts A–M for existing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitals/hospital units excluded from IPPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1886(d)(1)(B), certain hospitals and units are excluded from IPPS: IRF hospitals and units; LTCHs; IPF hospitals and units; children's hospitals; cancer hospitals; extended neoplastic disease care hospitals; hospitals located outside the 50 States, DC, and Puerto Rico; and RNHCIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded hospitals may have separate PPSs (IRF, LTCH, IPF) or continue to be paid on a reasonable cost basis subject to a rate-of-increase ceiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment basis for excluded hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Children's hospitals, cancer hospitals, hospitals located outside the 50 States/DC/PR, RNHCIs, and extended neoplastic disease care hospitals continue to be paid solely under a reasonable cost-based system, subject to a rate-of-increase ceiling on inpatient operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing regulations governing payments to excluded hospitals are in 42 CFR parts 412 and 413.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS scope and dual-rate/site-neutral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: LTCH PPS applies to hospitals described in section 1886(d)(1)(B)(iv) and, beginning FY 2016, became a dual rate payment system generally paying site-neutral payment rate unless patient meets criteria for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LTCH PPS regulations located at 42 CFR part 412, subpart O; annual LTCH PPS updates issued with IPPS updates beginning Oct 1, 2009.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAH payment basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sections 1814(l), 1820, and 1834(g), payments to Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) for inpatient and outpatient services are generally based on 101 percent of reasonable cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable cost determined under section 1861(v) and regulations at 42 CFR part 413.

rubrics_metrics.name: GME direct cost payments and IME adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals with approved GME programs are paid for direct GME costs per section 1886(h); IME payments provide additional payment for higher patient care costs based on the residents-to-beds ratio and a congressionally set multiplier (IME formula multiplier is 1.35 for FY 2008 and thereafter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations regarding IME adjustment are at 42 CFR 412.105; direct GME payment amount is based on number of residents in the cost reporting period and hospital's costs per resident in a base year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital definition and payment adjustment sliding scale
rubrics_metrics.description: For FYs 2019 through 2026 and portion of FY 2027 (Oct 1–Dec 31, 2026), a subsection (d) hospital qualifies as a low-volume hospital if it is more than 15 road miles from another subsection (d) hospital and has less than 3,800 total discharges during the fiscal year; the Secretary determines an additional percentage increase using a continuous linear sliding scale from an additional 25% payment for ≤500 discharges to 0% for >3,800 discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects amendments under section 1886(d)(12) as extended by CAA, 2026 through Dec 31, 2026; CMS proposes conforming regulatory amendments to reflect statutory extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG annual adjustment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(4)(C) requires the Secretary to adjust DRG classifications and relative weights at least annually to account for changes in resource consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments reflect changes in treatment patterns, technology, and other factors that change relative hospital resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG classification change request process (MEARIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties submit MS-DRG classification change requests via MEARIS (Medicare Electronic Application Request Information System); deadline for FY 2027 requests was October 20, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEARIS provides resources and technical support (public resources page and Contact form); burden subject to Paperwork Reduction Act (OMB control number 0938-1431, expiration 01/31/2029). CMS will inform requestors via MEARIS if a request cannot be considered in the upcoming fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of test GROUPER software and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is providing a test version of the ICD-10 MS-DRG GROUPER Software, Version 44, draft Definitions Manual, draft Definitions of Medicare Code Edits (MCE) Manual, and supplemental mapping files to allow the public to test and analyze FY 2027 proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test software reflects proposed GROUPER logic and new/modified code updates; supplemental mapping files (Tables 6P.1a/6P.1b) include mapped Version 44 codes and deleted Version 43 codes for testing; draft MCE manual (Version 44) and resources available on CMS website; public may submit questions/comments to MSDRGClassificationChange@cms.hhs.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCE manual composition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Definitions of Medicare Code Edits (MCE) Manual comprises Chapter 1: Edit code lists (listing each edit, explanation, and applicable codes) and Chapter 2: Code list changes (summarizes additions/deletions from prior release).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft MCE manual provided for public review; finalized MCE reflected in annual IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision criteria for creating/splitting MS-DRG severity subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding whether to split a base MS-DRG into severity subgroups (MCC/CC/NonCC), CMS applies five criteria: volume (Criteria 1 & 2), average cost (Criteria 3 & 4), and reduction in variance (Criteria 5). All five must be met for a three-way split; if failure, CMS evaluates two-way splits (1_23 or 12_3) using the same principles and may choose the two-way split with the highest R2 if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new MS-DRG creation CMS typically evaluates the most recent year of MedPAR data; for splitting existing base MS-DRGs, CMS typically analyzes two years of MedPAR data to avoid decisions based on an isolated year's fluctuation. CMS prefers not to create a new MS-DRG unless it would include a substantial number of cases. If a request specifically asks for a particular two-way split, CMS evaluates both two-way splits but does not also evaluate a three-way split in response to that specific request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic metrics for evaluating resource consumption and clinical distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considers whether resource consumption and clinical characteristics of a patient set are significantly different than the remainder of the MS-DRG by evaluating average costs and lengths of stay, both absolute and percentage differences, variation within groups (consistency vs. driven by extremes), and the number of patients with given characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS relies on clinical factors and cost/LOS analyses and generally prefers not to create new MS-DRGs for small volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity factors that may require extended analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Some requested MS-DRG changes (especially since ICD-10 implementation) may require more extensive research and cannot be fully considered within the upcoming fiscal year's rulemaking; such requests may involve multiple MS-DRGs, overlapping logic across MDCs, special logic combining diagnosis and procedure codes, complex code clusters, or multiple logic lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS informed requestors in December 2025 via MEARIS if a request could not be considered for FY 2027; such requests may be deferred to future rulemaking cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for public comment on MS-DRG proposed changes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS invites public comments on each MS-DRG classification proposed change and on proposals to maintain certain existing MS-DRG classifications included in the FY 2027 proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public may use the test GROUPER and documentation to analyze impacts; submission channels include MEARIS and CMS-listed contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to repeal alternative pathway for new technology/add-on and device pass-through applications
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to repeal the alternative pathway for new technology add-on payment and OPPS device pass-through applications, requiring all applicants to demonstrate they meet all eligibility requirements to receive add-on payments and/or pass-through payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See discussion in section II.E.7. of the preamble for rationale and implementation details; public input on proposed changes and status of new technologies (including town hall inputs and FDA-authorized technologies) is presented in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index update and adjustment methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed FY 2027 wage index update uses wage data from cost reporting periods beginning in FY 2023, includes calculation and implementation of an occupational mix adjustment based on the 2022 Occupational Mix Survey, proposed application of rural, imputed and frontier State floors, a proposed transition for discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy, proposed adjustments based on hospital redesignations/reclassifications, proposed commuting-pattern-based adjustments, and proposed labor-related share for applying the FY 2027 wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS details calculation, analysis, and proposed implementation steps in section III of the preamble; changes address multiple technical and policy factors affecting wage index values.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSH uncompensated care payment methodology proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed calculation of Factor 1 and Factor 2 of the uncompensated care payment methodology; proposed methodology for determining Factor 3 (same as FY 2026); and proposed methodology for determining the amount of interim uncompensated care payments using the average of the most recent 3 years of discharge data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section IV of the preamble for detailed methodology proposals and how the factors interact in the uncompensated care payment calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed inpatient hospital market basket and related IPPS payment updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed inpatient hospital market basket update for FY 2027, proposed updated national and regional case-mix values and discharges (for RRC status), and proposed conforming amendments reflecting statutory extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These proposals are included in section V of the preamble and affect IPPS operating updates and case-mix calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed prohibition on unlawful discrimination by GME and NAH programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirements to prohibit unlawful discrimination by graduate medical education programs and nursing and allied health education programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among proposed regulatory clarifications and changes in section V to ensure equal access and compliance by educational programs receiving Medicare payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed criteria modifications for identifying new residency programs and GME/IME payment clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed modifications to criteria for identifying new residency programs for purposes of direct GME and IME payments; proposed clarifications of the methodology for calculating direct GME and IME payments following a teaching hospital merger; and notice of closure of two teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals aim to clarify eligibility and payment adjustments in program creation, merger, and closure contexts; details in section V of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed NAH education program MA add-on rates and cost allocation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed nursing and allied health education program Medicare Advantage add-on rates and direct GME MA percent reductions for CY 2024; and proposed changes to regulations for determining net costs of approved NAH education programs and procedures for allocating indirect NAH costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects Medicare Advantage payment treatments and internal accounting/allocation methods for NAH education costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed immunotherapy case payment adjustment update
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed update to and revision of the payment adjustment for certain immunotherapy cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among IPPS operating cost proposals in section V; CMS provides rationale and estimated impacts in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed changes to CMS quality-based programs (HRRP, HVBP, HACRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to the requirements of the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program, Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program, and Hospital-Acquired Condition Reduction Program along with updated estimates of their financial impacts for FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS updates proposed measures and estimates impacts; see section V for details and for solicitation of comments on measure and policy proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural Community Hospital Demonstration Program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of and proposed changes relating to implementation of the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration Program in FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are included in section V and invite comment on demonstration design, participation, and payment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy governing capital-related IPPS costs for FY 2027
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed payment policy requirements for capital-related costs and capital payments to hospitals for FY 2027 (discussed in section VI of the preamble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS addresses methodology, factors, and regulatory clarifications specific to capital payments in section VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments to certain excluded hospitals: rate-of-increase percentages and FCHIP
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to payments to certain excluded hospitals for FY 2027 and proposed continued implementation of the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) Demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details in section VIII of the preamble and the Addendum describing rate-of-increase limits and demonstration continuation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS payment rate components and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to LTCH PPS Federal payment rates, factors, and other payment rate policies for FY 2027, including adjustments for the wage index, labor-related share, COLA, high-cost outliers (fixed-loss amounts), and LTCH cost-to-charge ratios (CCRs) for both the standard Federal and site-neutral payment rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are described in section VIII of the preamble and section V of the Addendum; CMS proposes specific factor updates and solicits comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed changes to quality data reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to the requirements for the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program, PCH Quality Reporting Program, Long-Term Care Hospital Quality Reporting Program, and requirements pertaining to eligible hospitals and CAHs participating in the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details are in section IX of the preamble; proposals may change reporting measures, data submission processes, or eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitations for comments and RFIs on models and episodes (TEAM, ASC, physician ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is soliciting comment on proposed changes to TEAM affecting episodes, quality measure assessment, and pricing methodology; soliciting an ambulatory surgical center episode RFI; and an RFI on voluntary hospitals with physician ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section X.A–X.C detail the scope of solicitations; responses inform potential future policy or model development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed revision to provider-based location criteria (§413.65)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to the provider-based location criteria regulations applicable to off-campus facilities or organizations (§413.65).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in section X.B of the preamble; changes would affect provider-based billing eligibility for off-campus locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals for the CJR-X Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for the CJR-X Model with policies affecting participation, episodes, quality measure and assessment, pricing methodology, model overlap, financial arrangements, waivers of Medicare Program requirements, data sharing, and APM options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed in section X.C; CMS outlines model policy proposals and solicits stakeholder comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO/HCL cost reconciliation and standard acquisition charges (SACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to reconcile non-renal organ acquisition costs for independent organ procurement organizations (IOPOs) and histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs), and to require Medicare Administrative Contractors to establish, adjust if necessary, and publish IOPO non-renal standard acquisition charges (SACs) and HCL testing rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also proposes to codify longstanding Medicare reasonable cost reimbursement policies, clarify/codify cost allocation principles, and codify discretionary Administrator review of CMS reviewing official determinations with respect to appeals under §413.420(g) for IOPOs and HCLs. See section X.D for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addendum procedures for determining prospective payment rates and outlier thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Addendum, CMS sets forth proposed changes to amounts and factors for determining FY 2027 prospective payment rates for operating and capital costs for acute care hospitals, establishes threshold amounts for outlier cases, and addresses update factors for rate-of-increase limits for certain excluded hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections II and III of the Addendum cover operating and capital rate calculations; section V covers excluded hospitals' update factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact analysis and Appendix B update factor recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A provides analysis of the impact of proposed changes on affected entities; Appendix B (per sections 1886(e)(4) and (e)(5)) provides CMS recommendations of appropriate percentage changes for FY 2027: a single average standardized amount for all areas, target rate-of-increase limits for excluded hospitals, and LTCH PPS payment rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices include quantitative impact estimates and CMS's recommended update factors for stakeholder review.
